task_message:
Case L36: segment the lipomatous soft-tissue tumor on this T1-weighted MRI.

Volume: 235x251x221 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
The case is complete. 

**Summary of what I did:**
1. **Located the lesion** with `seg_open` and contact sheets in all three planes — a large, well-defined lipomatous (fat-intensity on T1) mass occupying the anterolateral compartment of the thigh, spanning nearly the full craniocaudal extent of the volume.
2. **Initial segmentation** with two positive point prompts inside the mass on axial slice 110, giving a 737 mL mask.
3. **Verified and corrected** with targeted zooms (axial 15/100/140/165/170/180/185/195, coronal 112/136/159, sagittal 149/180/213), filled internal holes, and ran a model refinement which cleaned the boundary (720 mL, single component).
4. **Reviewed the automatic candidates** (C1–C3) — all three were merely the surrounding normal subcutaneous fat ring around the mask, so I rejected them.
5. **Saved** the final mask after inspecting the five-slices-per-plane final review.

Final result: one connected lipomatous mass, 720.2 mL, following the fat/muscle and fat/subcutaneous boundaries in all three planes, with medium confidence (the main residual uncertainties being the internal displaced muscle band at the medial margin and the tapering distal tip near the knee).
